title: New deal: same-day security call
summary: Security questions are blocking a pilot. The customer asks for a call later the same day and confirms an approved pilot budget.
showcases: A same-day meeting can't be confirmed as future from a date-only call record. If the model resolves it to the call date, the meeting-v1 validator removes the date (DATE_NOT_FUTURE), and the meeting goes to review either way
Safe autonomous write: an explicitly approved budget, with last year's figure heard but not written

turns.text: Thanks for the time, Tamsin. You mentioned over email that security questions were holding things up.
Right. Before anything else moves, our security engineer wants to walk through your SSO setup and audit logging with someone technical.
That makes sense. I can bring our solutions engineer. When would suit you?
Sooner is better. Could the two of you do a call today at 3:30? I'll pull our security engineer in.
Yes, 3:30 today works. I'll send a video link in the next few minutes.
Great. On the commercial side, last year we only had $25,000 for tooling pilots. This year we have $60,000 approved for this pilot, so budget is settled.
Good to know. I'll have a pilot proposal ready right after the security call.

budget.why: "This year we have $60,000 approved for this pilot" is an explicit, current, approved budget for this purchase, stated in digits. Last year's $25,000 is HISTORICAL, so it's ABSTAIN and appears in the ledger.
risks: If the classifier treats $25,000 as CURRENT (unlikely), the candidates conflict and the field becomes ASK.

decisionMaker.why: Nobody says who signs. A Head of IT title alone doesn't establish final authority. Expected: no candidate, or an INDIRECT/NONE candidate → ABSTAIN or ASK.
risks: The extractor might propose Tamsin from her title. The classifier should label that NONE or INDIRECT; INDIRECT would make it ASK.

nextMeeting.why: Agreed, explicit, but same-day. The call record is date-only, so a same-day time can't be shown to be in the future. Two paths both end in ASK: (A) the extractor resolves the date to the call date, meeting-v1 fires DATE_NOT_FUTURE and removes it, VALUE_UNVERIFIED; (B) the extractor leaves the date null, UNDERSPECIFIED_VALUE. Only path A demonstrates the validator, and we can't make the model take it.
risks: Path B (date null) means the validator doesn't fire; Ardent then shows the stored experiment trace for the validator demonstration.

Known meeting-v1 gap, reported, not fixed: if the extractor resolved "today" to a LATER date (for example the next day), no meeting-v1 rule would catch it, because "today" only satisfies DATE_UNSUPPORTED. The policy would then ACT. We don't expect this, but if a recording shows it, it will be preserved and reported.

dryRuns.label: Path A: extractor resolves 'today' to the call date (validator fires)

evidence.quote: last year we only had $25,000 for tooling pilots
This year we have $60,000 approved for this pilot, so budget is settled.
Could the two of you do a call today at 3:30?

dryRuns.label: Path B: extractor leaves the date null (validator has nothing to check)
